items.title: Death toll in Gokarna tragedy rises to three
points: The death toll in the tragedy at Gokarna in Uttara Kannada has risen to three with the body of the missing tourist being fished out on Monday.
A team of 16 tourists comprising techies from Bengaluru had come on a holiday to a resort near Dubbanashasi beach on Sunday, and six of them entered the sea for swimming.
According to sources, they were caught in the waves and began drowning.

While three persons, Nishanth D.V., Goutam, and Mohammed Kasim from Bengaluru, were rescued by local fishermen, Shobha Das, 23, of Jamshedpur breathed his last on the spot, and Mohammad Akram, 23, from Bengaluru passed away on the way to the hospital.
Another techie, identified as Vishwesh A.K., 23, from Bengaluru, went missing.
A joint search launched by the Gokarna Police, Coast Guards, and local fishermen yielded results during the early hours of Monday, and his body was fished out.
The Gokarna Police have registered a case.

items.title: Broad Industry Coalition Urges Permanent Suspension of Costly U.S. Port Fees on China-Linked Ships
points: In an October 30 letter to U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, the coalition welcomed the proposed two-month extension of the Section 301 vessel fee suspension through January 9, 2027, but called on Washington to go further and eliminate the charges…

The groups argue that reinstating the fees would add another layer of costs to supply chains already struggling with elevated freight rates, equipment availability challenges and uncertainty in global trade.

Because Chinese-built ships account for a significant share of global shipping capacity, the coalition warned that the impact would extend well beyond Chinese shipping companies, affecting vessel deployments and transportation costs for American importers…

The latest industry appeal follows the Trump administration’s October 23 proposal to extend the suspension through January 9, 2027, as Washington and Beijing continue negotiations over China’s dominance of the maritime, logistics and shipbuilding sectors.
The fees were originally imposed in October 2025 before being suspended the following month under a broader U.S. -China trade agreement.

items.title: Anbumani opposes proposed ₹5 hike in Aavin milk prices
points: PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss has urged the Tamil Nadu government to reject Aavin’s reported proposal to increase milk prices by ₹5 per litre, stating that it would place an additional burden on poor and middle-class families.
In a statement, he said the proposed hike followed a recent ₹6 per litre increase in the procurement price of milk supplied to Aavin, which was expected to widen the cooperative’s losses.
Acknowledging that Aavin incurred a loss of ₹89.80 crore in 2025-26, he said increasing retail prices was not the only way to address its financial difficulties.
Pointing out that Aavin milk was considerably cheaper than products sold by private dairies, he said a ₹5 increase would amount to a hike of up to 12.5%.

He called for addressing administrative inefficiencies and corruption in Aavin’s management and providing government subsidies to compensate for losses incurred in supplying milk at affordable prices.

items.title: Ernst Russ AG sells MV “Mirror”
points: Ernst Russ AG sold the container vessel MV “Mirror”.
The vessel, built in 2007 with a capacity of 803 TEU, is scheduled to be handed over to its new owner in January 2027.
The parties have agreed not to disclose the purchase price.
As the handover will not take place until 2027, the sale has no impact on the assets, financial position and earnings for the 2026 financial year.
Earlier this year, the company sold the container vessels MV “EF Emira” and MV “EF Emma” while expanding its fleet with multipurpose vessels and product-/chemical tankers.
The most recent example is the delivery of the newbuild MT “Farrie Russ” on 27 October 2026.
With these steps, Ernst Russ is pursuing the goal of a diversified, modern fleet with a balanced risk profile in terms of vessel segments, charter durations and counterparts.
“The sale of MV ‘Mirror’ reflects the disciplined approach we take in developing the Ernst Russ AG fleet,” says Joseph Schuchmann, Co-CEO and Chief Commercial Officer of Ernst Russ AG.

points: Corvus Energy, global market leader in marine energy storage systems (ESS), is partnering with naval electrical solutions company, Servintel, to provide specialized, local-based technical support and service capabilities for Corvus Energy clients in Argentina.
Working with Servintel in Argentina is an important part of that solution—enabling specialized local service, backed by global expertise.
Notably, this service scope includes the world’s largest battery-electric ship, the Buquebus China Zorrilla ferry, which entered operations in Argentina in October this year.

Servintel, a South American-based company headquartered in Buenos Aries, was founded in 1979 with the primary goal of delivering efficient, innovative electrical and electronic solutions to demanding markets in the naval and industrial sectors.

With a multidisciplinary team of experienced professionals specialized in marine electrical and electronic systems, including automation, control systems, and energy management—Servintel is well equipped to support Corvus Energy clients in Argentina.
A notable exception— the world’s largest 100% electric ship, with zero direct emissions during navigation—recently entered service in Argentina.

points: A regional workshop on ships’ routeing and ship reporting systems is taking place in Lima, Peru (26-30 October).

The workshop aims to strengthen participant’s understanding of how these measures can enhance maritime safety and protect the marine environment, and how proposals for new or revised systems can be submitted to IMO.

The programme covers the principles, design criteria and procedures for establishing ships’ routeing and ship reporting systems, drawing from the General Provisions on Ships’ Routeing and the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS)…

Participants are receiving guidance on how to prepare proposals for submission to IMO’s Sub‑Committee on Navigation, Communications and Search and Rescue (NCSR), and on how proposals are evaluated before being considered for adoption by the IMO’s Maritime…

Under SOLAS Chapter V (Safety of navigation) and relevant provisions of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), IMO is responsible for establishing and adopting ships’ routeing systems and ship reporting systems at the international…

items.title: Qatar, Saudi Arabia condemn attack on Pakistan-bound LNG tanker in Gulf waters
points: Qatar and Saudi Arabia have condemned an attack on a liquefied natural gas (LNG) tanker reportedly carrying cargo destined for Pakistan through Gulf waters, calling it a “dangerous act” that threatened the security of global energy supplies.

Pakistan had negotiated with Iran to secure safe passage for the LNG carrier, Al Mayeda, before the ship was attacked near the Strait of Hormuz last week, Bloomberg reported on Sunday, citing people with direct knowledge of the matter.

The Marshall Islands-flagged vessel was sailing toward the waterway loaded with LNG from Qatar when it came under fire, the people said, asking not to be named as they were not authorized to speak to the media.

“The Ministry of Foreign Affairs affirms that the State of Qatar reserves its right to take all necessary measures, in accordance with international law and the UN Charter, to protect its assets and safeguard its vessels and their crews,” it said.

items.title: WISTA International elects new president and champions cross-border collaboration at conference in Kuala Lumpur
points: WISTA International has elected Céline Mortier as its new President.
The former WISTA Belgium President and CEO of maritime provider Bogerd Martin was formally appointed to the new role as part of this week’s WISTA International AGM and Conference 2026.
The appointment follows two terms as President for Elpi Petraki, who brought four years at the helm of the global association to a close at the event, staged in Kuala Lumpur, 28-30 October.

Co-hosted by WISTA Hong Kong SAR China, WISTA Malaysia and WISTA Singapore, this year’s AGM and Conference brought together over 250 professionals from across the global maritime, logistics and trading sectors.

Four new NWAs were announced during the AGM – Bahamas, Egypt, Montenegro and the Philippines – bringing its total number of national associations to 64, while WISTA member numbers worldwide exceed 6,500.

Maryana Stober, Diruni Chanmugam and Amsha Gengan were also appointed to the WISTA International Executive Committee, after four years of dedicated service from Jemilat Mahamah, Dafne Anghelidis and Raimah Chowdhury.

items.title: Imported iron ore margin narrows to 0.04 yuan/mt
points: The average imported iron ore margin narrowed from 8.72 yuan/mt to 0.04 yuan/mt in the latest period, weighed down mainly by lower port spot prices and higher freight.
Iron ore currently faces rising supply and falling demand.
The latest SMM data showed iron ore stocks at 35 major ports across China at 148.05 million mt, up 300,000 mt from the previous survey, marking a slight build.
Average daily port outbound volume fell 35,000 mt to 3.175 million mt.
With hot metal output expected to decline further next week, iron ore demand may continue to weaken, capping upside for prices.
Macro factors also lack a stronger driver, and prices are expected to remain range-bound next week.
News on long-term contract negotiations and environmental production curbs in northern China could still disrupt prices.
The import margin is likely to narrow gradually in the short term as freight rates rise.

items.title: Greece Factory Activity Slows for 2nd Month
points: The S&P Global Greece Manufacturing PMI fell to 53.3 in October 2026 from 54.0 in September, marking a second consecutive monthly decline but remaining firmly in expansionary territory.
Output, new orders and employment continued to rise amid improving market demand, with production recording its strongest growth since July.
However, new order growth slowed to its weakest pace since May.
Disruptions linked to the Middle East conflict continued to weigh on the sector, with supply chains under pressure and input delivery delays remaining widespread amid higher transport costs.
Meanwhile, lower warehouse inventories and stronger production contributed to a second consecutive monthly decline in backlogs of work.
Despite the ongoing expansion, price pressures remained elevated.
Confidence in the outlook subsequently deteriorated, falling to a five-month low.

points: The air quality is likely to be in the 'very poor' category for the next three days, as per the Central government’s Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi.

Stage 2 of the GRAP mandates NCR State governments to enhance vehicle parking fees to discourage use of private vehicles.

The GNCTD (Delhi government) and NCR State governments also have to “stagger timings for public offices and municipal bodies in the National Capital Territory of Delhi and the districts of Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar”.
Considering the restrictions on vehicles, the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has decided to run additional trips on weekdays.
While the DMRC was running 20 trips since October 28, when the GRAP-1 was enforced, 20 more trips will be run now.

Your financial system is fully controlled and supported by foreigners.

items.title: Fire breaks out at Vizag's HPCL refinery; no casualties, say cops
points: A fire broke out at the Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) refinery in Gajuwaka industrial area of Andhra Pradesh's Visakhapatnam late on Monday night, police said.
“The fire is believed to have erupted at the sulphur pitch tank of the refinery's Residue Upgradation Facility (RUF) within the HPCL refinery premises.
The tank caught fire, resulting in eruption of flames and thick smoke,” Malkapuram inspector of police Prakash Rao told reporters.
“Flames quickly spread to nearby areas, sending thick clouds of black smoke into the sky and engulfing the surrounding locality,” an employee of HPCL said.
Soon after receiving information about the fire, the refinery's internal firefighting teams rushed to the spot and launched firefighting operations.
“Though the fire stations in other parts of the city were alerted, there was no need for them, as the internal fire tenders themselves brought the fire under control,” Prakash Rao said.
The exact cause of the fire accident will be known only tomorrow, the HPCL employee said.

items.title: Village guard, wife die of bullet wounds in Jammu’s Reasi
points: A Village Defence Guard (VDG) and his wife died of bullet wounds in Jammu’s Reasi district on Monday (November 2, 2026).
The victims were identified as Javed Ahmed, a resident of Brailkund, Manjikote, Bagodass, and his wife Shaheen Akhter.
A woman was left dead in Kishtwar’s Chatroo area after a VDG opened fire in 2025.
In 1995, Village Defence Committees were constituted in 10 districts of the Jammu region.
However, after the Dangri attack in Rajouri in 2023, which left six civilians dead and 15 others injured, the Centre revived these groups and renamed them VDGs.
Prior to 2006, around 26,567 locals were recruited into Village Defence Committees in the Jammu region.
According to official figures, 160 criminal cases involving Village Defence Committees members were filed in the Jammu region.
The incident took place in the Nowshera sector at 11:30 a.m. near a forward post close to the LoC.

items.title: Upcoming IPO: Coal India unit South Eastern Coalfields files papers – How much funds to be raised and other key facts
points: South Eastern Coalfields Ltd (SECL), a subsidiary of state-owned Coal India Ltd, has filed preliminary papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) to launch its initial public offering (IPO), marking another step in the government's…

The proposed public issue will comprise an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 66.81 crore equity shares by promoter Coal India, with no fresh issue component, according to the Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) dated November 1.
The IPO could raise as much as $800 million, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
According to the DRHP, citing a Crisil report, SECL produced 176.29 million tonnes of coal in FY26, accounting for 16.94% of India's total coal production.
It contributed 22.95% to Coal India's overall production during the financial year.
As of April 1, 2026, SECL had total geological coal resources of approximately 47.55 billion tonnes, representing around 11.50% of India's total coal geological resources.

Pawan Kalyan has directed officials to remain on high alert as cyclone Murasu approaches the coast, even as the State is yet to recover from the damage caused by cyclone Arnab.

At a review meeting with senior officials of the Panchayat Raj and Rural Development and Rural Water Supply Departments on Monday, Mr. Kalyan said the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had warned of extremely heavy rain in Nellore, Prakasam,…

In view of the forecast of intense rainfall, he stressed the need to evacuate people living in low-lying areas to safer locations, ensure proper coordination among departments, minimise hardship and prevent loss of life.
Officials informed the Deputy Chief Minister that the cyclone was initially forecast to cross the coast between Bapatla and Machilipatnam.

Heavy rain was already lashing Nellore, Prakasam, Bapatla, Tirupati and Markapuram districts under the influence of the cyclone.

This will be the first visit by Mr. Misri to Nepal since Prime Minister Balendra Shah took charge in March this year following the election that was conducted under an interim government.

Vietnam remains an important strategic partner for India under its Act East Policy and broader Indo-Pacific vision.

items.title: Search continues for missing auto-rickshaw driver
points: Updated - November 02, 2026 10:40 pm IST - THIRUVANANTHAPURAM The search for a 68-year-old auto-rickshaw driver, Vidyadharan, who was swept away after his vehicle plunged into a waterlogged canal at Vembayam a day ago, continued on Monday.
Fire and Rescue Services personnel from Thiruvananthapuram and Nedumangad, along with scuba diving teams and local residents, have been conducting an extensive search operation.
Vidyadharan and his wife, Lathakumari, a former panchayat member, were returning from a wedding reception on Sunday evening when the accident occurred.
Heavy rainfall had caused the canal to overflow, making it difficult to distinguish the road from the waterway.
While negotiating a turn near the Chirrakkonam canal at Vettinad, the vehicle reportedly veered into the canal, causing both persons to fall into the river.
Search operations began soon after the accident, with fire personnel and local residents conducting searches until around 11 p.m.
Scuba diving teams have been divided into two groups and are searching the canal and its adjoining waterways.

items.title: Railway officer found dead in Agra DRM office; family alleges suicide due to 'toxic' work culture
points: A 32-year-old railway officer was found dead in one of the chambers at the divisional railway manager's Office in Agra, officials said on Monday.
The deceased, Abhishek Singh Kushwaha, was posted as an assistant operations manager (AOM) in the Agra railway division.
His body was found on a sofa in an office chamber at around 11 pm on Sunday, police said.
Kushwaha's wife and mother have alleged that a toxic work culture and mental harassment by a senior official drove him to take his own life.

items.title: Speeding car triggers three-vehicle crash at Golf Course Road underpass in Gurugram; FIR filed
points: A major road accident occurred at the underpass near the Sector 42-27 intersection on Golf Course Road in Gurugram, allegedly due to high-speed and reckless driving, police said on Monday.
In the incident, one car overturned, while another collided with the wall of the underpass.
The car that triggered the accident also crashed into the wall, authorities stated.
A video circulating on social media shows a speeding car colliding with two vehicles ahead of it inside the underpass.
Acting on the video, Head Constable Parmila and her team arrived at the scene to inspect the site and question witnesses present at the time, police said.
The investigation revealed that the accident occurred in the early hours of October 31.
An unidentified driver was allegedly operating a vehicle at high speed and in a negligent manner, which led to collisions with two cars ahead, damaging all three vehicles.
An FIR has been filed against the unidentified driver at the Sushant Lok police station as of Sunday.

items.title: Gold, silver prices rebound from multi-month lows as crude oil retreats; what is driving the recovery?
points: Gold and silver prices recovered in Monday’s trade after hitting multi-month lows, as easing inflationary pressures amid a sharp retreat in crude oil prices supported sentiment.
The December gold futures contract on the MCX gained ₹2,039 per 10 grams to touch the day’s high of ₹1,40,524.
Silver prices also attempted a recovery, with the futures contract rising ₹5,543 per kg to ₹1,84,675.

The rebound came after silver logged back-to-back monthly losses, with October marking its steepest monthly decline, at 20%, or ₹44,574 per kg and during the period, it touched the lowest level in 10 months.

Crude oil prices extended the decline on Monday, with Brent crude futures dropping 7% to below $105 a barrel, as hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the US-Iran conflict eased concerns over further supply disruptions.
Silver has lost 56% of its value from its record high of ₹4,20,048 per kg.

items.title: Meghalaya: Paul Lyngdoh returns as minister; Metbah quits cabinet after UDP collapse
points: Meghalaya’s United Democratic Party (UDP) president Metbah Lyngdoh lost his cabinet berth following the political upheaval that reduced his party to a one-man outfit.
Meanwhile, former party colleague Paul Lyngdoh returned to the Conrad K Sangma government as a minister, this time representing the National People’s Party (NPP).
Paul, the West Shillong legislator who left the UDP for the NPP along with two other party colleagues, was sworn in as a cabinet minister by governor CH Vijayashankar at Lok Bhavan on Monday evening.
He was allocated the tourism portfolio, which he previously held before being dropped in the September 2025 cabinet reshuffle.

His induction follows Metbah’s resignation from the cabinet on October 31, after 11 of the UDP’s 12 legislators left the party, with eight joining the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and three moving to the NPP.

items.title: New Harley Davidson Sprint 440 Debuts – Made In India Cruiser By Hero
points: Harley-Davidson has officially unveiled the Sprint 440, expanding its small-capacity motorcycle portfolio with a cruiser developed in partnership with Hero MotoCorp.
Harley-Davidson has confirmed a spring 2027 introduction in the United States, with final assembly at its York, Pennsylvania facility.
Harley Davidson is also working on X350T for India.
The Sprint name also reconnects Harley-Davidson with its lightweight motorcycle history, having first appeared in 1961.
Power comes from a 440cc air- and oil-cooled single-cylinder engine, producing 26.7 bhp at 6,000 rpm and 38 Nm at 4,000 rpm.
Claimed combined fuel efficiency is approximately 34 kmpl, although real-world results will depend on riding conditions.
Equipment includes a circular 3.5-inch colour TFT instrument cluster, full-LED lighting and a USB-C charging port positioned above the headlamp.
The Sprint 440 has been announced at a starting price of £4,995 in the UK (Rs 6.34 lakh), while US pricing is around $6,000 (Rs 5.68 lakh).

items.title: Michelin Launches X Multi Energy Z2 Truck Tyre In India, Claims Up To 13% Better Fuel Efficiency
points: Michelin has launched its new-generation X Multi Energy Z2 truck and bus tyre in India, claiming that it is the country's most fuel-efficient tyre in the All Position category.
The new Michelin X Multi Energy Z2 focuses on three key areas that directly affect the operating costs of commercial vehicle fleets: fuel efficiency, tyre life and durability.
Michelin claims that the tyre can deliver fuel savings of up to 6% in the 295/80R22.5 tubeless size and up to 13% in the 295/90R20 tube-type size, compared to leading competition.
The X Multi Energy Z2 is expected to deliver up to 25% more tyre life compared to the nearest competition in the same size.
The tyre also gets Michelin's Duracore technology, with the company claiming 11% better summit strength compared to leading competition.
Its fuel-efficiency testing was conducted on an Ashok Leyland 16-wheeler 4825 truck on the Namakkal-Dindigul highway between June 22 and 28, 2026.
The tyre is manufactured at Michelin's Chennai facility and uses up to 30% recyclable materials.

points: Binance has resumed USDT, USDC, and ETH withdrawals on Ethereum, alongside BNB withdrawals on BNB Smart Chain, following the October 29 attack that reportedly resulted in $6.3 billion in stolen cryptocurrency.

points: Standard Chartered expects the $6.3 billion Binance hack to encourage greater adoption of decentralised exchanges as investors reassess the risks of centralised platforms.
